idea-plugin.name: EFCore Visualizer
idea-plugin.description:
View the execution plan of an Entity Framework Core query while you debug, without leaving Rider. Supports SQL Server, PostgreSQL, Oracle and SQLite.

This is the Rider version of the EFCore Visualizer for Visual Studio. It shows the same plan pages.

Requirements

  • Rider 2025.1 or newer.
  • An app that uses EF Core 7 or newer, on .NET 6 or newer.
  • Allow property evaluations and other implicit function calls turned on, in Settings | Build, Execution, Deployment | Debugger. It's on by default.

Usage

  1. Debug your app and pause it, for example at a breakpoint, where a query is in scope.
  2. In Variables or Watches, right-click the query (an IQueryable from EF Core, or a DbSet) and choose Visualize Query Plan.

The plan opens in an editor tab. The menu item appears only on EF Core queries, whatever the variable's declared type.

  • Each variable gets its own tab, so you can compare plans side by side.
  • Visualizing the same variable again brings its tab to the front. If the query changed in the meantime (another Where or OrderBy, a new query assigned, a different parameter value), the tab gets the new plan.

Important: the query runs

For SQL Server, PostgreSQL and Oracle, the plugin shows the actual plan, so it runs the query in your app, on your app's connection and transaction. Getting the plan takes as long as the query, and your app stays paused until it finishes. Rider stops evaluations after 1 second by default; while it gets a plan, the plugin raises that limit to 30 seconds for the debug session (or keeps yours, if it's higher). For SQLite, the plugin only asks for the estimated plan (EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN), so the query doesn't run.

When there's no plan

If the plugin can't get the plan, a short warning says why, and the tab shows the query's SQL instead. Visualizing the variable again tries the plan again.

Known issues

  • Your app must run on the same machine as Rider: debugging an app in Docker, WSL or on another machine isn't supported yet. .NET Framework apps aren't supported.
  • If your app uses Application Insights, getting the plan can fail with "Cannot evaluate expression since the function evaluation requires all threads to run". The same happens in Visual Studio (#28). Disable Application Insights while debugging.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.0.0: first release.

  • Visualize Query Plan in the Variables and Watches context menu, for EF Core queries and DbSets.
  • Plans for SQL Server, PostgreSQL, Oracle and SQLite, the same pages as the Visual Studio extension. When there's no plan, the query's SQL, with the reason.
  • One tab per variable, reused while its query is unchanged.
  • Progress with the elapsed time while a plan is fetched. The debugger's evaluation limit is raised to 30 seconds meanwhile.
  • Rider 2025.1 and newer.
